key_insight: A zero-shot, agentic LLM workflow can extract lung pathology synoptic fields from narrative reports with strong performance, approaching a supervised baseline.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual abstraction burden for cancer staging and tumor registry data entry, especially where annotated training data is limited.
method: Compared five open-source generative LLMs on 13 College of American Pathologists synoptic fields.
Used a zero-shot, agentic extraction workflow instead of task-specific fine-tuning.
Benchmarked against a supervised GatorTron NER-RE baseline with a registry-aligned evaluation.
evidence_signal: The supervised baseline reached Micro-F1 0.960, while the best zero-shot model (GPT-OSS-20B) achieved Micro-F1 0.893 with recall 0.949 on lung resection pathology reports.
watch_item: Performance is still below the supervised baseline, so real-world deployment would need careful validation for accuracy, edge cases, and consistency across report styles.
paper_title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives
